questions.question_hindi:
POSH अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 19 के अंतर्गत नियोक्ता के कर्तव्यों के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
I. नियोक्ता को कर्मचारियों को संवेदनशील बनाने के लिए नियमित अंतराल पर कार्यशालाएं एवं जागरूकता कार्यक्रम आयोजित करने चाहिए।
II. नियोक्ता को आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) को शिकायत के निपटारे और जांच संचालन हेतु आवश्यक सुविधाएं उपलब्ध करानी चाहिए।
III. नियोक्ता को आंतरिक शिकायत समिति के समक्ष प्रत्यर्थी और गवाहों की उपस्थिति सुनिश्चित करने में सहायता करनी चाहिए।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?
options_hindi: केवल I और II
केवल II और III
केवल I और III
I, II और III

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the duties of an employer under Section 19 of the POSH Act, 2013:
I. The employer must organize workshops and awareness programmes at regular intervals for sensitizing employees.
II. The employer must provide necessary facilities to the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) for dealing with the complaint and conducting an inquiry.
III. The employer must assist in securing the attendance of the respondent and witnesses before the ICC.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II, and III
questions.explanation_english:
Section 19 of the POSH Act, 2013 sets forth the comprehensive statutory duties of an employer:
- Section 19(c): Organise workshops and awareness programmes at regular intervals for sensitising employees with the provisions of the Act and orientation programmes for members of the Internal Committee (Statement I is correct).
- Section 19(d): Provide necessary facilities to the Internal Committee or the Local Committee, as the case may be, for dealing with the complaint and conducting an inquiry (Statement II is correct).
- Section 19(e): Assist in securing the attendance of respondent and witnesses before the Internal Committee or the Local Committee (Statement III is correct).
Since all three statements represent explicit legal obligations under Section 19, option (D) is the correct answer.
questions.explanation_hindi:
POSH अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 19 में नियोक्ता के कर्तव्यों को स्पष्ट रूप से परिभाषित किया गया है:
- धारा 19(c): कर्मचारियों को अधिनियम के प्रावधानों के प्रति संवेदनशील बनाने के लिए नियमित अंतराल पर कार्यशालाओं और जागरूकता कार्यक्रमों का आयोजन करना तथा आंतरिक समिति के सदस्यों के लिए अभिविन्यास कार्यक्रम आयोजित करना (कथन I सही है)।
- धारा 19(d): आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) को शिकायत के निस्तारण और जांच के संचालन हेतु आवश्यक सुविधाएं उपलब्ध कराना (कथन II सही है)।
- धारा 19(e): आंतरिक समिति या स्थानीय समिति के समक्ष प्रत्यर्थी (आरोपी) और गवाहों की उपस्थिति सुनिश्चित कराने में सहायता करना (कथन III सही है)।
अतः तीनों ही कथन धारा 19 के अंतर्गत नियोक्ता के वैधानिक दायित्व हैं, इसलिए सही उत्तर (D) है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (d) I, II, and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 19 outlines comprehensive duties for employers, including organizing orientation workshops and awareness programs, providing necessary logistical facilities to the committee for conducting inquiries, and securing the attendance of the respondent and witnesses before the committee during formal proceedings. All three listed statements represent statutory obligations.

questions.question_hindi:
आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) द्वारा संचालित की जाने वाली जांच प्रक्रिया के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
I. पक्षों को ICC के समक्ष अपना प्रतिनिधित्व करने के लिए विधिक व्यवसायियों (वकीलों) को लाने की अनुमति होती है।
II. यदि प्रत्यर्थी बिना किसी वैध कारण के लगातार तीन सुनवाइयों में अनुपस्थित रहता है, तो ICC के पास एकपक्षीय (एक्स-पार्टी) निर्णय लेने की शक्ति है।
III. एकपक्षीय आदेश पारित करने अथवा कार्यवाही समाप्त करने से पहले ICC द्वारा संबंधित पक्ष को 15 दिन की अग्रिम लिखित सूचना देना अनिवार्य है।
IV. ICC द्वारा की जाने वाली जांच को 60 दिनों के भीतर पूरा किया जाना आवश्यक है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?
options_hindi: केवल I और II
केवल II और III
केवल III और IV
केवल I, II और IV

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the inquiry procedure conducted by the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC):
I. The parties are permitted to bring legal practitioners to represent their case before the ICC.
II. The ICC has the power to make an ex-parte decision if the respondent fails to appear for three consecutive hearings without sufficient cause.
III. The ICC must serve a 15-day advance written notice to the party concerned before passing an ex-parte order.
IV. The inquiry of the ICC must be concluded within 60 days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
III and IV only
I, II, and IV only
questions.explanation_english:
Let us analyze each statement based on the POSH Act, 2013 and POSH Rules, 2013:
1. Statement I is incorrect: Rule 7(6) of the POSH Rules, 2013 expressly prohibits legal representation, stating that 'The parties shall not be allowed to bring any legal practitioner to represent them in their case at any stage of the proceedings before the Complaints Committee.'
2. Statement II is correct: Under Rule 7(5), the Complaints Committee has the right to terminate the inquiry proceedings or to give an ex-parte decision on the complaint, if the complainant or respondent fails, without sufficient cause, to present herself or himself for three consecutive hearings convened by the Chairperson or Presiding Officer.
3. Statement III is correct: The proviso to Rule 7(5) mandates that such termination or ex-parte order cannot be passed without giving a notice in writing, 15 days in advance, to the party concerned.
4. Statement IV is incorrect: Under Section 11(4) of the POSH Act, 2013, the inquiry must be completed within 90 days, not 60 days.
Therefore, only Statements II and III are correct.
questions.explanation_hindi:
पॉश अधिनियम, 2013 तथा पॉश नियमावली, 2013 के आधार पर कथनों का विश्लेषण:
1. कथन I गलत है: नियम 7(6) के अनुसार, कार्यवाही के किसी भी चरण में पक्षों को आंतरिक शिकायत समिति के समक्ष अपना पक्ष रखने हेतु किसी विधिक व्यवसायी (वकील) को लाने की अनुमति नहीं दी जाएगी।
2. कथन II सही है: नियम 7(5) के तहत यदि शिकायतकर्ता या प्रत्यर्थी पर्याप्त कारण के बिना लगातार तीन सुनवाइयों में उपस्थित नहीं होता है, तो समिति को जांच समाप्त करने या एकपक्षीय (ex-parte) निर्णय देने का अधिकार है।
3. कथन III सही है: नियम 7(5) के परंतुक (proviso) के अनुसार, ऐसी समाप्ति या एकपक्षीय आदेश पारित करने से पूर्व संबंधित पक्ष को 15 दिन की अग्रिम लिखित सूचना देना अनिवार्य है।
4. कथन IV गलत है: अधिनियम की धारा 11(4) के अनुसार जांच 90 दिनों के भीतर पूरी की जानी चाहिए, न कि 60 दिनों में।
अतः केवल कथन II और III सही हैं (विकल्प B)।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (b) II and III only

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Statutory rules prohibit parties from bringing legal practitioners to represent them before the committee. An ex-parte decision or dismissal can occur if a party fails to present themselves for three consecutive hearings without sufficient cause, provided a fifteen-day advance written notice is served. Inquiries must be completed within ninety, not sixty, days.

questions.explanation_english: Section 19 of the POSH Act, 2013 delineates the duties of an employer. questions.question_english: The POCSO Act, 2012 was enacted primarily to address gaps in the existing penal laws and to give effect to the provisions of which international convention?
options_english: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC)
Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW)
International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights
questions.explanation_english: The Preamble to the POCSO Act, 2012 explicitly states that the Government of India acceded on 11th December, 1992 to the Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC), adopted by the General Assembly of the United Nations. Under Articles 19 and 34 of the UNCRC, State parties are obligated to take all appropriate legislative, administrative, social, and educational measures to protect children from all forms of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, and violence. To fulfill this international commitment and replace the inadequate, non-child-centric provisions of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, Parliament enacted the POCSO Act, 2012.
questions.explanation_hindi: POCSO अधिनियम, 2012 की उद्देशिका में स्पष्ट रूप से उल्लेख है कि भारत सरकार ने 11 दिसंबर 1992 को संयुक्त राष्ट्र महासभा द्वारा अंगीकार किए गए 'बाल अधिकार अभिसमय' (UNCRC) का अनुमोदन (accession) किया था। इस अभिसमय के तहत सभी सदस्य देशों के लिए बच्चों को लैंगिक शोषण और दुर्व्यवहार से बचाने हेतु प्रभावी विधिक उपाय करना अनिवार्य था। तत्कालीन भारतीय दंड संहिता (IPC) में बच्चों के अनुकूल प्रक्रिया और लड़के-लड़कियों दोनों के लिए व्यापक यौन अपराध संरक्षण की कमी थी, जिसे दूर करने और UNCRC के अधिदेश को पूरा करने हेतु POCSO अधिनियम, 2012 लागू किया गया।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (b) UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: (UNCRC) India ratified the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1992. questions.question_english: Under the POSH Act, 2013, what happens if the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) arrives at the conclusion that the allegation against the respondent has NOT been proved?
options_english: The employer must still transfer the respondent as a mandatory precautionary measure
The ICC recommends to the employer that no action is required to be taken in the matter
The ICC must recommend punishing the woman for wasting committee time and resources
The case is automatically forwarded to the Local Complaints Committee for a fresh inquiry
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 13(2) of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (POSH Act), where the Internal Committee (ICC) or Local Committee (LCC) arrives at the conclusion that the allegation against the respondent has not been proved, it submits its inquiry report to the employer (or District Officer) recommending that no action is required to be taken in the matter. This statutory recommendation officially closes the administrative inquiry without any penalty or adverse record against the respondent. Furthermore, under Section 14, an inability to substantiate an allegation or inadequate evidence does not automatically render the complaint false or malicious; penal action against a complainant can only be initiated if deliberate malicious intent and falsification of evidence are strictly established.

questions.explanation_english:
Assertion (A) is correct: The POSH Act, 2013 explicitly extends its jurisdiction to the unorganized sector (enterprises employing fewer than 10 workers) and domestic workers employed in dwelling places, primarily governed through the mechanism of Local Committees (LC) established under Sections 6 and 7. Section 2(a)(ii) specifically defines an aggrieved woman in relation to a dwelling place.
Reason (R) is also correct: Section 2(o)(v) of the Act embodies the doctrine of 'notional extension' of the workplace, defining it to include any place visited by the employee arising out of or during the course of employment, including transportation provided by the employer.
However, Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A). The legislative reason why domestic workers and the unorganized sector are covered is not because employees travel during employment (R), but because the statute explicitly enacted separate provisions (Sections 2(e), 2(p), and Section 6) to guarantee social justice and universal workplace safety for women in unorganized private households and small firms. Therefore, both statements are legally true, but R is not the causal explanation of A.

questions.explanation_english: This constitutes an offence exclusively under the POCSO Act, 2012. The reasons are two-fold: First, the POSH Act, 2013 (Section 2(a)) defines an 'aggrieved woman' and is gender-specific, protecting only women against workplace sexual harassment; it does not extend protection to male victims. Second, the POCSO Act, 2012 is entirely gender-neutral. Under Section 2(1)(d) of the POCSO Act, a 'child' is defined as any person below the age of 18 years, irrespective of sex. Under Section 11/12 (sexual harassment of a child) and Section 9(c) (aggravated sexual assault committed by a teacher or person on the staff of an educational institution having authority or trust over the child), demanding sexual favours from a 16-year-old boy constitutes an aggravated sexual offence under POCSO. questions.explanation_english: Under Section 6(1) of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (POSH Act), every District Officer is required to constitute a Local Committee (formerly known as the Local Complaints Committee or LCC) in each district. The statute specifically mandates that where an establishment has fewer than 10 workers or where the complaint of sexual harassment is against the employer himself, the aggrieved woman must file her complaint directly with the Local Committee. The Internal Complaints Committee (ICC/IC) cannot inquire into allegations against the employer because the employer exercises administrative and financial control over the workplace and the ICC members, creating an unavoidable conflict of interest and violating the fundamental principle of natural justice ('nemo judex in causa sua' — no one should be a judge in their own cause). In the context of school administration, if allegations are leveled against the school owner, manager, or head of the managing committee/trust who acts as the legal employer, the matter falls under the exclusive jurisdiction of the district Local Committee.

आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) नियोक्ता के अधीन कार्यरत कर्मियों से मिलकर बनती है। अतः यदि शिकायत स्वयं नियोक्ता के विरुद्ध हो, तो नैसर्गिक न्याय के सिद्धांत ('कोई भी व्यक्ति अपने ही मामले में न्यायाधीश नहीं हो सकता') के तहत हितों का टकराव (Conflict of Interest) उत्पन्न होता है। विद्यालय प्रबंधन में यदि स्कूल प्रबंधक, ट्रस्टी या संस्था प्रमुख (जो नियोक्ता की श्रेणी में आते हैं) के विरुद्ध आरोप हो, तो जांच LCC द्वारा ही की जाती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Local Complaints Committee (LCC)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under Section 6(1), when a complaint of workplace sexual harassment is against the employer themselves, the Internal Complaints Committee cannot handle the matter due to inherent conflict of interest. In such cases, the aggrieved woman must submit her complaint directly to the district Local Complaints Committee for inquiry.

At the child's residence or a place of the child's choice
In the Principal's office at the educational school premises
In the formal district court premises during working hours
questions.explanation_english: Section 24(1) of the POCSO Act, 2012 specifies that the statement of the child shall be recorded at the residence of the child or at a place of the child's choice. Furthermore, the child should never be detained at the police station overnight for any reason whatsoever. Conducting the examination at the child's home or a comfortable chosen location shields the minor from the intimidating atmosphere of a police station and helps reduce secondary trauma.
questions.explanation_hindi: पॉक्सो अधिनियम, 2012 की धारा 24(1) के अनुसार, बच्चे का बयान अनिवार्य रूप से बच्चे के निवास स्थान पर या बच्चे की पसंद के किसी अन्य स्थान पर दर्ज किया जाना चाहिए। इसके अतिरिक्त, बच्चे को किसी भी परिस्थिति में रात भर पुलिस स्टेशन में नहीं रखा जा सकता। पुलिस स्टेशन के डरावने या तनावपूर्ण माहौल से बच्चे को बचाना और उसे अपने सुरक्षित वातावरण में सहजता से अपनी बात कहने का अवसर देना इस कानून का मुख्य ध्येय है।

questions.question_english: Section 16 of the POSH Act, 2013 strictly prohibits the publication or disclosure of which of the following information to the public, press, or media?
options_english: The information regarding the justice secured to any victim of sexual harassment without disclosing the identity
The total number of sexual harassment cases filed in the organization's annual report
The composition of the Internal Complaints Committee
The identity and addresses of the aggrieved woman, respondent, and witnesses
questions.explanation_english: Section 16 of the POSH Act, 2013 strictly prohibits the disclosure or publication of the contents of the complaint, the identity and addresses of the aggrieved woman, respondent, and witnesses, any information relating to conciliation and inquiry proceedings, or the recommendations of the Internal/Local Committee to the public, press, or media in any manner. However, the proviso to Section 16 explicitly allows information regarding the justice secured to any victim to be disseminated, provided that it does not disclose the name, address, identity, or any other particulars that may lead to the identification of the aggrieved woman or witnesses. Display of ICC composition and aggregated annual statistics are also permissible.
questions.explanation_hindi: पॉश अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 16 के अनुसार, सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2005 में किसी बात के होते हुए भी, शिकायत की विषय-वस्तु, व्यथित महिला, प्रत्यर्थी और गवाहों की पहचान एवं पते, सुलह तथा जांच कार्यवाही से संबंधित किसी भी जानकारी तथा समिति की सिफारिशों को जनता, प्रेस अथवा मीडिया में प्रकाशित या संप्रेषित करने पर पूर्ण प्रतिबंध है। हालांकि, धारा 16 के परंतुक के तहत पीड़िता और गवाहों की पहचान छिपाकर न्याय सुरक्षित किए जाने संबंधी सामान्य जानकारी दी जा सकती है। समिति के गठन तथा वार्षिक रिपोर्ट में मामलों की कुल संख्या का प्रकटीकरण प्रतिबंधित नहीं है। अतः विकल्प D सही उत्तर है।

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: woman, respondent, and witnesses Section 16 prohibits disclosing the identity, address, or identifying details of the aggrieved woman, respondent, and witnesses, as well as inquiry proceedings or committee recommendations, to the public, press, or media. questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the institutional safety protocols and POCSO guidelines recommended for schools:
I. Every school must establish an internal Child Abuse Monitoring Committee (CAMC) / Child Safety Committee.
II. Teachers and staff members should be trained not to ask probing, suggestive, or leading questions if a child discloses sexual abuse.
III. To safeguard the school's reputation and avoid panic among parents, the administration may resolve the matter internally without reporting it to the police.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II, and III
questions.explanation_english:
Statements I and II are correct, while Statement III is completely false and unlawful:
- Statement I is correct: Under NCPCR and CBSE POCSO safety guidelines, schools are mandated to establish a Child Abuse Monitoring Committee (CAMC) or Child Safety Committee to maintain vigilance, oversee child safety, and manage grievance mechanisms.
- Statement II is correct: Staff members must be trained to receive disclosures with empathy and calmness, strictly avoiding interrogative, judgmental, or leading questions that could traumatize the child or distort factual recall.
- Statement III is incorrect: Under Section 19 and Section 21 of the POCSO Act, 2012, reporting any knowledge or apprehension of child sexual abuse to the police/SJPU is mandatory. Concealing an offence or failing to report it under the pretext of protecting institutional reputation or handling it internally is a criminal offence punishable under Section 21 with imprisonment of up to six months or one year (for in-charge/heads) or fine or both.
questions.explanation_hindi:
कथन I और II सही हैं, जबकि कथन III पूर्णतः गलत और गैर-कानूनी है:
- कथन I सही है: NCPCR तथा CBSE के पॉक्सो दिशा-निर्देशों के अनुसार, प्रत्येक विद्यालय में बाल सुरक्षा की निगरानी एवं शिकायतों के निवारण हेतु 'बाल उत्पीड़न निगरानी समिति' (CAMC) अथवा बाल संरक्षण समिति का गठन किया जाना अनिवार्य है।
- कथन II सही है: शिक्षकों एवं कर्मचारियों को संवेदनशील बनाया जाना आवश्यक है ताकि वे प्रकटीकरण (disclosure) के समय बच्चे से अनावश्यक, दबाव डालने वाले या भ्रामक प्रश्न (leading questions) न पूछें, जिससे बच्चे पर मानसिक दबाव न पड़े और साक्ष्य प्रभावित न हों।
- कथन III गलत है: पॉक्सो अधिनियम की धारा 19 के तहत मामले की सूचना पुलिस/SJPU को देना अनिवार्य वैधानिक दायित्व है। संस्था की प्रतिष्ठा बचाने के नाम पर रिपोर्ट न करना धारा 21 के तहत एक संज्ञेय अपराध है, जिसके लिए संस्था प्रमुख को कारावास व जुर्माने का दंड हो सकता है। अतः केवल कथन I और II सही हैं। इसलिए विकल्प A सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (a) I and II only

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Schools must form child abuse monitoring committees and train staff to avoid asking probing or leading questions when receiving disclosures. Concealing incidents or withholding reports from police to protect institutional reputation violates Section 19 and Section 21, attracting severe criminal penalties for institutional leadership under statutory provisions.
